questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to challenge myself and go out of my comfortzone by going on an exchange alone.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to experience university life in England, since it's kind of similar to USA. There's a lot more focus on the activities outside of just school which I really liked. It gave you a good opportunity as an exchange student to meet a lot of new people in different settings.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved everything about the exchange, the only detractors are actually before I left Denmark because the time up until was quite stressful. There were a lot of deadlines all the time and it was also really hard to find accommodation in Newcastle.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Newcastle University made it quite easy, but it just takes a lot of time to research it all because there are a lot of things you need to remember before you leave from home.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Newcastle University was so helpful and I felt so comfortable with them from the beginning. They made it very clear that if I had any issues or questions they were always available, so I really appreciated that. My contact person for the exchange, Emilia, was so helpful and welcoming. I was also given a mentor from year 3 and a buddy group with other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult because there is a lack of housing in many UK university cities right now, even though Newcastle is filled with student housing everywhere you look.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived alone in a studio apartment in a student housing accommodation. It was really nice to have my own space, but it also means that you have to put yourself out there even more and actively seek friendships in class or at activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really lucky that I found something off campus because many places would only let to students who could commit to a full year contract. Furthermore, many of my friends who got accommodation through the university didn't know were they were gonna live or even if they had a place to live upon arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered for courses online when I applied for Newcastle University, but when I arrived at my host institution there were a lot more choices available to me, which was a really nice surprise. You just had to send an email to the office confirming your choice of courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My contact person Emilia gave us some good advice on which courses she would recommend and then we had 2 weeks to change our minds again if we wanted to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry if none of the courses you have chosen the first time seem interesting to you. A lot more will probably become available when you arrive at the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it a bit easier to study in Newcastle, probably because of the structure of classes. We mostly had lectures of 1 hour and then every other week we would have a seminar in each course. In the seminars there are only 10-12 people which makes it very intimate but in a really good way.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One of my courses was with the stage 2 students and the rest were with stage 3 students. But I didn't really feel any difference in the complexity of the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I felt like I learned a lot more even though I had less classes. Probably because it was so intense and compact when you were in class, but then you also knew it would be over quickly so it was easier to focus completely throughout the lectures and seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Criminal Law
Law and Gender
Law and Literature

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Its expensive if you want to take the train to another city like Edinburgh or London, so book ahead of time to get the best prize.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general I would say that eating out was less expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every activity you could dream of was available through the host institution. In the beginning of the semester they have a social fare were many of the activities have a booth so you can get a feel of the many possibilities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the 20 minutes society. It was really fun and different because once a week you would get a text at some point saying that you have 20 minutes to get to a random address which could be anything from a bar to an activity.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: ESN has many great tours during the weekends, so sign up for some of them so you get to know more people and explore the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I feel like it was quite easy since their wasn't a huge culture difference between England and Denmark. Also the English people from the north are known to be very welcoming and friendly which I really feel like they lived up to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think its easier to socialize with local students on an exchange in an English speaking country because there is no language barrier. My advice would be to sign up for some of the activities so you have something in common to start the conversation. Or just try to sit next to someone in class and introduce yourself, the rest will follow.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing that comes to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open and put yourself out there. 
The first few days are hard, but it will get easier once you have established some friendships.
Time flies faster than you think, so get the most out of every weekend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up for the ESN Facebook group and WhatsApp group chat so you don't miss out on any of the events from the beginning. They usually host a welcome party for all international students which is a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I feel like I learned a lot about myself and have become more confident in myself and when I meet new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the first welcome meeting because you feel so alone and haven't met anyone yet. But my advice would be to just find someone in the crowd and go up and sit next to them and start a conversation. When you have overcome that the first time it will be much easier the second time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
